source.text:
Win-rate figures vary widely by source (8% to 36%) because they measure different things: significant-winner-per-test vs decisive-rate vs research-prequalified. Always carry the definition and the sample with the number. The most conservative and best-sourced anchor is "about 10-20% of well-run tests produce a significant winner" (Kohavi, Thomke/Ghosh, Optimizely).

The DRIP 36.3% and platform 12-20% figures are not in conflict once you note DRIP pre-qualifies hypotheses with research and reports a looser win definition.

Several sources are dated 2026 SEO/agency posts. They are used only for uncontroversial, cross-checked facts (tooling landscape, Shopify plan limits). Anything statistical is anchored to Tier 1-2 primary sources.

Flag for the knowledge base: the Shopify checkout-extensibility position is evolving. As of late 2025 native checkout A/B testing is limited to Plus theme/Rollouts and a few Checkout Blocks apps; re-verify this yearly because Shopify is actively adding extensibility features.
